Sc RN Aseq Workflow Parameters Descripti: Low quality cells were filtered out based on low or extremely high UMI counts, low gene counts, and high mitochondrial read contributions in a cell type, protocol, and chemistry dependent manner. Samples with extremely low numbers of recovered cells were excluded as failed. Variable gene selection, dimensionality reduction using principal components analysis, Leiden clustering on a shared nearest neighbor graph, and UMAP visualization were performed. Cells were annotated through a combination of automated annotation, marker gene, and CNV assessment. Tools used include Cumulus, Seurat, inferCNV, and SingleR.

For each sample, we obtained the unfiltered feature-barcode matrix per sample by passing the demultiplexed FASTQs to Cell Ranger v6.0.2 <U+2018>count<U+2019> command using default parameters and the prebuilt GRCh38 genome reference (refdata-gex-GRCh38-2020-A; GRCh38 and Ensembl 93). Seurat v4.1.0  was used for all subsequent analysis. First, a series of quality filters were applied to the data to remove those barcodes which fell into any one of these categories recommended by Seurat: too few total transcript counts (<300); possible debris with too few genes expressed (<200) and too few UMIs (<1,000); possible more than one cell with too many genes expressed (>10,000) and too many UMIs (>10,000); possible dead cell or a sign of cellular stress and apoptosis with too high proportion of mitochondrial gene expression over the total transcript counts (>10%). Doublets were filtered out using Scrublet (https://github.com/AllonKleinLab/scrublet). Scrublet was run on each sample separately with the following parameter settings: expected_doublet_rate=0.06, min_counts=2, min_cells=3, min_gene_variability_pctl=85, n_prin_comps=30. The doublet score threshold was adjusted manually. We constructed a Seurat object using the unfiltered feature-barcode matrix for each sample. Any merged analysis or subsequent subsetting of cells/samples underwent the same scaling and normalization method. Cells were clustered using the original Louvain algorithm and top 30 PCA dimensions via <U+2018>FindNeighbors<U+2019> and <U+2018>FindClusters<U+2019> (with parameters: resolution = 0.5) functions. The resulting merged and normalized matrix was used for the subsequent analysis. For each sample, we obtained the unfiltered feature-barcode matrix per sample by passing the demultiplexed FASTQs to cellranger v6.0.2 (cellranger-arc v2.0.0 for 10X multiome libraries) <U+2018>count<U+2019> command using default parameters and the prebuilt GRCh38 genome reference (refdata-gex-GRCh38-2020-A; GRCh38 and Ensembl 98). Seurat v4.1.0  was used for all subsequent analysis. First, a series of quality filters were applied to the data to remove those barcodes which fell into any one of these categories recommended by Seurat: too few total transcript counts (<300); possible debris with too few genes expressed (<200) and too few UMIs (<1,000); possible more than one cell with too many genes expressed (>80,000) and too many UMIs (>10,000); possible dead cell or a sign of cellular stress and apoptosis with too high proportion of mitochondrial gene expression over the total transcript counts (>10%). Doublets were filtered out using Scrublet (https://github.com/AllonKleinLab/scrublet). Scrublet was run on each sample separately with the following parameter settings: expected_doublet_rate=0.06, min_counts=2, min_cells=3, min_gene_variability_pctl=85, n_prin_comps=30. The doublet score threshold was adjusted manually. Each sample was scaled and normalized using Seurat<U+2019>s <U+2018>SCTransform<U+2019> function to correct for batch effects (with parameters: vars.to.regress = c("nCount_RNA", "percent.mito"), return.only.var.genes = F). Cells were clustered using the original Louvain algorithm and top 30 PCA dimensions via <U+2018>FindNeighbors<U+2019> and <U+2018>FindClusters<U+2019> (with parameters: resolution = 0.5) functions. Any merged analysis or subsequent subsetting of cells/samples underwent the same scaling and normalization method.
